text:
prod-monitor-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in container restarts for runtime-pool-usw2 (GPU nodes). 18 restarts in 4m, OOMs reported during prefill phase. Error signature: CUDA outOfMemory / sigkill. Investigating.
sre-oncall: I'm paged, taking this. Looking at pods now.
eng-ops: seeing the same from metrics: request concurrency dropped and tail latency up. Likely long-context prefill.
emily (eng-runtime): grabbing logs for the failing containers. Can you paste a sample stack?
sre-oncall: logs (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T09:12:02Z runner[pid=2345]: prefill: allocating KV cache 6.3GB
2026-03-15T09:12:02Z runner[pid=2345]: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (0x700)
2026-03-15T09:12:02Z runner[pid=2345]: fatal: SIGKILL (OOM) - container terminated
```
emily (eng-runtime): yep that's the OOM during prefill. Looks like large prompt windows ( > 65k tokens ) in a small-quantized model path.
ryan (eng-infra): infra-bot shows node flapping on gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-18, kubelet restarted on both. Likely noisy neighbor/overcommit plus large prefill spikes.
prod-monitor-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-002 (auto). Paging oncall.
sre-oncall: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) disable prefill on the runtime pool for now, 2) cordon problem nodes, 3) move traffic to lower-memory model variants. Any objections?
emily (eng-runtime): agree. Quick temporary knob: set PREFILL_ENABLED=false for runtime-pool-usw2 route. I can flip that. That should avoid allocating huge KV caches and prevent restarts, but will increase latency for very long prompts.
ryan (eng-infra): I'll cordon gpu-node-{17,18} and drain pods to healthy nodes. Running: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.
eng-ops: note that draining might concentrate load and cause additional prefill pressure elsewhere. Recommend throttling concurrency on the runtime-pool before drain: `kubectl patch hpa runtime-pool --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2,"maxReplicas":4}}'` and set route concurrency to 1.
sre-oncall: executing sequence now: 1) set route PREFILL=false, 2) throttle concurrency to 1, 3) cordon & drain. I'll update when done.
(2m later)
sre-oncall: PREFILL toggled off for runtime-pool-usw2 via console. Concurrency set to 1. K8s drain started on gpu-node-17.
ryan (eng-infra): drain succeeded for gpu-node-17, cordoned. gpu-node-18 showing kernel logs for GPU reset, holding off draining until it stabilizes.
emily (eng-runtime): logs after PREFILL=false: no further immediate cuda OOMs in the pool; restarts dropped to 0 in the last 2m. Good sign.
carmen (customer-success): customers alerting. Which customers are affected and severity? We need a short summary for comms.
sre-oncall: Preliminary: 9 customers saw increased 5xxs or truncated responses in last 30m. Impact window started ~09:10 UTC. We mitigated heavy restarts by 09:18 with PREFILL off and draining. User-facing error rate is trending down.
prod-monitor-bot: Metric snapshot: peak container restarts 18 (09:12), 5xx rate +12% for affected routes, average p95 latency +240ms for fallback flow.
emily (eng-runtime): next steps (short term): 1) patch runtime to enforce a hard prefill token limit per-request (config: PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=20000) and add graceful fallback to streaming prefill; 2) add guarding in scheduler to avoid placing large-context requests on small-quantized nodes; 3) post-incident rollout of a soft quota for max_context per route. I'll open the PR.
ryan (eng-infra): medium term: audit noisy neighbor behavior and GPU isolation on those instance types, consider node labels for high-memory vs low-memory GPU flavors.
carmen (customer-success): I'll coordinate with top 5 affected customers with a brief: what happened, when we mitigated, how we're preventing recurrence. ETA for customer note?
sre-oncall: 30m for a short internal summary, 2h for a public-facing note.
postmortem-bot: Assigning postmortem owners: emily (eng-runtime) primary, ryan (eng-infra) secondary, sre-oncall for timeline.
emily (eng-runtime): taking postmortem. I'll collect request traces and the largest offending request IDs (we saw a few requests with 100k+ tokens). Will include reproducer and mitigation plan.
eng-ops: small follow-up: consider a temporary rate limit on max tokens per-request for public routes while we test the runtime patch. Could be a config flag in the gateway.
sre-oncall: Agreed. I've put a soft 60s/req and token cap of 50k at the gateway for runtime-pool-usw2.
carmen (customer-success): thanks all — I'll prepare comms and loop back once we have the postmortem draft.
emily (eng-runtime): FYI, I'll also add an alarm on prefill memory allocation spikes (threshold: >4GB prefill allocations per container within 1m) so we get earlier warnings.
sre-oncall: closing incident channel for now; monitoring for reoccurrence. If anything new, reopen here. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
